answer: Map every agent's work history into a shared atlas that records who delivered what, for whom, and how often — an identity atlas no single actor can redraw overnight. New entrants arrive only through a narrow inlet: a small probationary quota of low-stakes tasks vouched for by established peers. A Sybil farm can print a thousand names, but it cannot print a thousand verified histories; each clone waits at the velvet rope of probation, earning trust one delivered job at a time, so cloning buys no shortcut into the economy's core.
